messages:
marco: heads-up from today's onboarding run: sampleapp spiked 429s even though Console quota graphs looked fine. seems client-side behavior caused it.
eli: can you paste the sampleapp client config?
marco: trimmed snippet:
```js
// sampleapp quickstart client
const client = new RedwoodClient({
  windowSize: 5, // number of parallel pages
  maxConcurrentRequests: 12,
  pageSize: 64,
  prefetch: true,
  retry: { maxRetries: 2, baseDelayMs: 100 }
});
```
tara: windowSize 5 * 12 concurrency * prefetch can multiply into big short-lived QPS.
nate: is windowSize a per-session multiplier or global per process?
marco: per-session. during a 50-user perf run we saw local bursts where single session hit 30 concurrent calls for a few hundred ms.
kim: sdk parity note: go-sdk uses conservative defaults (windowSize=2, maxConcurrentRequests=6). js sampleapp drifted toward more aggressive defaults during a refactor.
eli: this is a classic backpressure gap; sampleapp should include leaky-bucket or token-bucket gate to smooth bursts.
marco: agreed. short-term fix: change quickstart to windowSize=2 and maxConcurrentRequests=6, and disable prefetch in default example.
tara: also add an observability hook so devs see "client.inflight" in console logs by default. cheap but reduces confusion.
nate: ops suggestion: add an X-Client-Burst header so server logs can correlate bursts to onboarding runs.
dev-bot: created issue #920: "sampleapp: smooth client windowing defaults + add inflight telemetry"
ops-bot: FYI support can increase account burst allowance temporarily, but that's a bandaid.
eli: medium-term: we should align defaults across sdks and expose an explicit "throughputMode: 'smooth' | 'aggressive'" option so people opt-in to high-concurrency.
kim: agree. will draft SDK parity PR to set smooth as default and add migration notes.
marco: adding a troubleshooting blurb to quickstart: "If you see short 429s during onboarding, lower windowSize/maxConcurrentRequests, disable prefetch, and enable jittered backoff."
tara: can we include a tiny code snippet for a local leaky-bucket wrapper?
marco: yes, i'll add a 6-line helper in the sampleapp repo.
eli: reminder: docs should explain how per-account token qps maps to client concurrency based on pageSize and typical token-per-request. many teams forget token math.
marco: will add a small table in the README showing tokens/request vs safe concurrency for small/medium/large accounts.
nate: great. thanks all — this should cut confusion and support tickets. :+1:
